item.description:
Partner clients are HubSpot customers that Solutions Partners have a sold or managed relationship with. Use the this API to manage your client base as well as sync client data between HubSpot and other systems. Note: you can only retrieve and update existing partner clients with this API. This API doesn't support creation or deletion.

Sync partner client data with third-party project management software.

[For more information, please refer to the documentation.](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/reference/api/crm/objects/partner-clients)

item.description:
Use properties to store information on CRM records. HubSpot provides a set of default properties for each CRM object, and you can also create and manage your own custom properties either [in HubSpot](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/properties/create-and-edit-properties) or using the properties API.

When creating properties, it’s important to consider how to architect your data. In many cases, creating custom properties for HubSpot's standard objects is the right course of action. However, there may be times when you'll need to create a separate [custom object](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/guides/api/crm/objects/custom-objects) with its own set of properties.  
  
[For more information, please refer to the documentation.](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/guides/api/crm/properties)

item.description:
# Projects API

Projects help you plan and organize your team’s work in one place with structured lists of tasks. Learn how to use the projects endpoints to get project data from your account.

Last modified: November 4, 2025In HubSpot, you can use the [projects object](http://knowledge.hubspot.com/records/understand-objects#projects) to help you manage your team’s work in one place. You can then use the projects API to programmatically retrieve and manage projects in your account.This guide refers to the projects object, not [HubSpot projects](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/help-and-resources/how-to-use-the-hubspot-projects-tool) or [developer projects](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/developer-tooling/local-development/hubspot-cli/project-commands).

## [​](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/guides/account/projects/guide?utm_source=devchangelog&utm_medium=blogpost&utm_campaign=202511_changelog_rollup&utm_content=3016#scope-requirements)Scope requirements

To use the projects API, you’ll need to authorize one of the following scopes for your app, based on the functionality you plan on using:

- `crm.objects.projects.read`: Retrieve project data.
    
- `crm.objects.projects.write`: Create, manage, and delete projects.
    
- `crm.schemas.projects.read`: Retrieve property settings for your projects.
    
- `crm.schemas.projects.write`: Update property settings for projects.
    

To view or manage [Sensitive Data and Highly Sensitive data](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/crm-sensitive-data/guide) for projects, you’d also need to authorize the following scopes:

- `crm.objects.projects.highly_sensitive.read`: View Highly Sensitive Data properties and values for projects.
    
- `crm.objects.projects.highly_sensitive.write`: Edit Highly Sensitive Data properties and values for projects.
    
- `crm.objects.projects.sensitive.read`: View Sensitive Data properties and values for projects.
    
- `crm.objects.projects.sensitive.write`: Edit Sensitive Data properties and values for projects.
    

[Please refer to our documentation for more information.](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/guides/account/projects/guide)

item.description:
The Partner Services API is a CRM API that allows you to manage partner service objects in HubSpot. It provides endpoints to:

- List and read partner services records
    
- Search for partner services
    
- Create associations between partner services and other CRM objects
    
- Batch read and update partner services
    

The API requires the `crm.objects.partner-services.read` scope for read operations and `crm.objects.partner-services.write` scope for write operations. It's available on all HubSpot product tiers (Free and above) for Marketing Hub, Sales Hub, Service Hub, Content Hub, and Data Hub.

The base endpoint is `/crm/v3/objects/partner_services`.

Refer to the documentation for additional details:

- [List partner services](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/crm-partner-services-v3/basic/get-crm-v3-objects-partner_services)
    
- [Search partner services](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/crm-partner-services-v3/search/post-crm-v3-objects-partner_services-search)
    
- [Associate partner services](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/crm-partner-services-v3/associations/put-crm-v3-objects-partner_services-partnerServiceId-associations-toObjectType-toObjectId-associationType)

item.description:
# Object library

Learn how to check whether or not objects in the object library are activated for use in a HubSpot account.

Scope requirements

As objects are added to the [object library](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/data-management/data-model-templates) in HubSpot, you can use the object library enablement endpoints to check whether or not an object is activated for use in a HubSpot account. The endpoints can check the status of an object, but you can only [activate or deactivate an object from within HubSpot](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/data-management/data-model-templates#view-the-object-library).If an object is enabled, an app will need the corresponding object [scopes](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/apps/legacy-apps/authentication/oauth-quickstart-guide#list-of-available-scopes) to access and manage records for the object. Learn more about creating and managing records [using the object APIs](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/guides/crm/understanding-the-crm).

## [​](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/crm-object-library-v3/guide#retrieve-enablement-statuses-of-all-objects-in-the-object-library)Retrieve enablement statuses of all objects in the object library

To check if all objects in the object library are activated in the account, make a `GET` request to `crm/v3/object-library/enablement`. Only objects which can be [activated or deactivated](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/data-management/data-model-templates#view-the-object-library) will be returned (i.e. contacts, companies, deals, and tickets will not be included).In your response, the `enablementByObjectTypeId` object will be returned with `objectTypeId` values and a value of `true` or `false` for each. If the value is `true`, the object is activated for use in the account. If the value is `false`, the object is deactivated. You can view each object’s `objectTypeId` value in [the table in this article](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/crm-property-validations-v3/guide#object-type-ids).For example, the following response shows an account where appointments and services are activated, but courses and listings are not.

```
//Example response
GET crm/v3/object-library/enablement
{
  "enablementByObjectTypeId": {
    "0-420": false,
    "0-421": true,
    "0-162": true,
    "0-410": false
  }
}

 ```

## [​](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/crm-object-library-v3/guide#retrieve-an-object%E2%80%99s-enablement-status)Retrieve an object’s enablement status

To check if a specific object is activated, make a `GET` request to `crm/v3/object-library/enablement/{objectTypeId}`. Refer to [the table in this article](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/crm-property-validations-v3/guide#object-type-ids) to find an object’s `objectTypeId`.The object’s `enablement` value will be returned as `true` or `false`. If the value is `true`, the object is activated for use in the account. If the value is `false`, the object is deactivated.For example, to check if appointments are activated in an account, make a `GET` request to `crm/v3/object-library/enablement/0-421`. If appointments are activated, the response will look like:

``` json
//Example response
GET crm/v3/object-library/enablement/0-421
{
  "enablement": true
}

 ```

[For more information, please refer to the API Documentation.](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/crm-object-library-v3/guide)

item.description:
The Schemas API is used to define and manage custom objects in HubSpot's CRM. Each object in HubSpot is defined by a schema, which includes:

- Configuration details: The object's name and ID
    
- Properties: The data the object can store
    
- Associations: Relationships with other objects
    

You can use the Schemas API to:

- Create custom objects with display properties, searchable properties, associations, and required properties
    
- Retrieve schema details for existing custom objects (via `GET /crm/v3/schemas`)
    
- Update object schemas (via `PATCH /crm/v3/schemas/{objectTypeId}`)
    

To manage an object's properties and association types after creation, you'd use the separate properties and associations APIs.

[Please refer to the API Documentation for additional details.](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/crm-schemas-v3/core/get-crm-object-schemas-v3-schemas)

item.description:
The BETA release of our [Forecast Read API](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/guides/sales/forecasts) is available to Sales Hub/Service Hub Professional and above. This new API enables customers to access their [forecast submissions](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/forecast/use-the-forecast-tool#submit-a-forecast) from HubSpot in a structured, queryable, and read-only format—ideal for Business Intelligence (BI) reporting, analytics, and integration into data warehouses. With this release, customers can now self-serve and programmatically retrieve forecast data, advancing data accessibility and integration capabilities.

#### What's changing?

- Read-only API access to all HubSpot forecasts, no UI changes required.
    
- Structured data retrieval: Query specific fields and integrate results into BI tools or data warehouses.
    
- Integration-ready: Use your authenticated app (crm.objects.forecasts.read scope) to access data programmatically.
    
- No UI/UX changes are required: Usage is fully programmatic through the API, and there are no changes to your HubSpot account via the [forecast tool](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/forecast/use-the-forecast-tool).
    
- Beta program: This feature is in BETA. By participating, you agree to [HubSpot’s Developer Terms and Beta Term](https://legal.hubspot.com/hs-developer-terms)s. Functionality and endpoints are subject to further development and changes.
    

**Usage**

Authorize your app with the crm.objects.forecasts.read and the oauth [scope](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/apps/legacy-apps/authentication/scopes) to use the endpoint. Below are the listed new read-only endpoints:

- **Get all forecasts:**
    

``` shell
GET /crm/objects/v3/forecasts?properties=property1,property2 

 ```

- **Get by ID:**
    

``` shell
GET /crm/objects/v3/forecasts/{id}

 ```

**Example response:**

``` json
{"results":[{"id":"475911884905","properties":{"hs_created_by_user_id":"2620022","hs_createdate":"2025-10-10T19:42:51.001Z","hs_lastmodifieddate":"2025-10-14T16:52:43.757Z","hs_milestone":"monthly","hs_object_id":"475911884905","hs_team_id":"39577840","hs_year":"2025"},"createdAt":"2025-10-10T19:42:51.001Z","updatedAt":"2025-10-14T16:52:43.757Z","archived":false}]}

 ```

For more details, please refer to the [HubSpot API Developer Documentation](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/guides/sales/forecasts#retrieve-forecast-types).
